$\frac{112}{12-5}$

**[1]**

$16\times2=32$

[1]

parts.problem_md:
A farmer has 45 horses and 20 cows.

i) Write this as a ratio of horses : cows. 
Give your answer in its simplest form.

[1]

ii) The farmer wants the ratio of horses : cows to equal 5 : 3. 
He keeps his 45 horses and buys some more cows.

Work out the number of cows he must buy.

[2]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Writing these two values as a ratio in the correct order*

$45:20$

> *The greatest common factor of *$45$* and *$20$* is *$5$

> *Divide both of these values by *$5$* to simplify the ratio*

$9:4$* ***[1]**

** **

ii) *The ratio of horses to cows in the form *$1:n$* is determined by dividing both parts of the ratio by *$5$

$\frac{5}{5}:\frac{3}{5}\,1:\frac{3}{5}$

> *Multiplying the number of horses (*$45$*) by the fraction *$\frac{3}{5}$* calculates the number of cows the farmer needs to own to in total to have the correct ratio*

$45\times\frac{3}{5}$

**[1]**

$=27$

> *Subtract the number of cows that the farmer already owns (20) from the number he needs to have (27) to determine how many cows the farmer must buy*

$27-20$

$7$ **[1]**
